newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dying man gets ireland's post-poll divorce.
newsitem.headline: Dying man gets ireland's post-poll divorce.

text.p: A dying man was on Friday granted Ireland's first divorce since it was legalised by a half per cent margin in a 1995 referendum.
The unnamed man, who is in his 60s, appealed to the High Court for a divorce even though a law approving it does not come into effect until next month.
The court, which heard his plea in camera, upheld his appeal that his constitutional rights had been infringed by the delay in the law coming to the statute books.
The man, who is terminally ill, has been separated from his wife for several years and wants a divorce to marry the woman with whom he has been living before he dies.
Divorce was legalised in Ireland, which is overwhelmingly Roman Catholic, after a bitterly contested referendum which was approved by a 0.56 percent majority.
Couples are entitled to divorce if they have lived apart for more than two years. In the past, they could get a legal divorce only in a foreign court.
